info.title: IntraVox API
info.description:
IntraVox is a modern intranet page builder for Nextcloud. This API provides endpoints for managing pages, media, navigation, comments, reactions, the Photo Story widget (galleries with EXIF, maps and lightbox) and the File Story widget (document libraries with MetaVox-aware filtering and federated-share awareness).

## Authentication failures and 429

Nextcloud applies brute-force protection to failed authentication at the platform level. Any authenticated endpoint here can therefore answer 429 Too Many Requests after repeated bad credentials from one address, whether or not that operation documents its own rate limit — and once tripped it keeps answering 429 even for correct credentials until the window expires.

This surprises automated clients most: a retry loop on a wrong token does not eventually succeed, it locks the address out. Treat 401 as terminal and fix the credentials rather than retrying.

get.description:
Returns the pages the current user may read, ordered by title then uniqueId.

**Response shape depends on the request.** Without `limit` or `cursor` the response is a bare array — unchanged from earlier versions — capped at 2000 entries. Send either parameter and the response becomes a paged envelope instead.

**Pagination is keyset, not offset.** The cursor encodes the sort key of the last row served, so a page created or deleted mid-walk cannot make the caller skip or repeat a row. There is deliberately no `offset` parameter.

200.description: A bare array by default, or a paged envelope when limit or cursor is sent.

X-IntraVox-Cap.description: The ceiling applied to an unpaginated response.

X-IntraVox-Truncated.description: `true` when the listing was cut off at the cap. Sent on unpaginated responses so a truncated answer can say so without changing shape.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Sending this switches the response to the paged envelope. Values above 500 are clamped, so paging cannot be used to exceed the listing cap.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response's `nextCursor`. Also switches the response to the paged envelope. A cursor this server did not issue is rejected with 400.

Returns a single page by its unique ID

The response carries `baseVersion`; send it back on PUT to avoid overwriting a concurrent edit.

put.description:
Updates an existing page

CONCURRENCY. A read returns `baseVersion`, the file's modification time at that moment. Send it back in the PUT body and a write that started from an older copy is refused with 409 instead of silently overwriting the other edit.

Omitting it is allowed and is NOT treated as a conflict — an importer or a script that never read the page has nothing to compare. That is a deliberate choice with a consequence worth knowing: a client that leaves `baseVersion` out gets last-write-wins. Interactive editors should always send it.

The value is never persisted; it is stripped from the payload before the page is written.

409.description: Conflict: the submitted baseVersion predates the stored file, so someone else saved while this copy was being edited. Re-read the page and re-apply the change; retrying the same body will keep failing.

post.description:
Adds the calling user's reaction and returns the complete new state.

Idempotent: adding a reaction the user already has, or removing one they never had, succeeds and returns the unchanged state. Safe to retry, and safe to fire from an optimistic UI.

404 covers both 'no such page' and 'no access to it', deliberately indistinguishable.

Rate limited to 30 per minute per user.

ONE REACTION PER USER, ALWAYS. Adding a reaction silently WITHDRAWS the user's previous one — this is not a configurable mode, it is unconditional. A client that treats this as purely additive will show a stale count for the emoji that was just removed, which is why every reaction endpoint returns the complete state instead of a delta: replace your local state, never increment it.

get.summary: Federated-aware preview proxy (shared by PhotoStory and FileStory)
get.description: Generates a thumbnail for a single file by id. Local files 302-redirect to NC core /core/preview so NC's own preview cache stays hot. Federated files (Files_Sharing\External\Storage) are fetched from the owner instance's publicpreview endpoint and cached in appdata. In-flight dedup ensures concurrent identical requests share one outbound call; a per-remote concurrency cap protects the owning NC instance from a stampede. Falls back to a 302 redirect to the matching mime-icon SVG when no preview can be produced. Rate-limited to 600 requests per user per minute.

A browser page, not a JSON resource — documented because it is the other half of a contract the API already refers to. GET /api/share/{token}/page/{uniqueId} can answer 401 with `passwordRequired: true`, and without this pair a client is told it needs a password and never told where to send it.

Password-protected shares serve a form here; unprotected ones serve the page directly.

200.description: The share page, or the password form.

404.description: No such share, or the token does not point into IntraVox.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded (60 per 60 seconds per client). Anonymous endpoints are limited per address rather than per user, so several visitors behind one NAT share the budget.

parameters.description: The public share token from the link.

post.description:
Form POST, not JSON. On success the password is kept in the session, which is what makes the subsequent /api/share/{token}/... calls succeed — so an API client needs a cookie jar here, not a token.

Failure is deliberately slow and throttled: the attempt is registered with brute-force protection and the response is delayed 100-300ms, so timing does not reveal whether a token exists.

returnQuery.description: Query string to restore after the redirect.

parameters.name: shareToken
parameters.description: The public share token from the link.

429.description: Too many attempts; brute-force protection has kicked in.

get.summary: Fetch items from an external feed or connection
get.description:
Fetches and normalises a feed. Which parameters matter depends on sourceType: 'rss' reads url, everything else reads connectionId plus the source-specific filters.

Rate limited to 30 requests per minute per user, because each call makes an outbound HTTP request on the server's behalf.

Failure is soft: a source that is unreachable, malformed or refuses the stored credentials returns 500 with an empty items array and a generic error string. The specific cause is logged server-side, never returned — it would disclose internal hostnames and credential state.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Clamped into 1..50; the result is capped at 50 regardless.

get.summary: Fetch a three-item preview while editing a widget

Identical to GET /api/feed/external but hard-limited to three items and with no limit parameter. Intended for the widget editor, so an author can confirm a source works before saving.

Unlike the other feed reads this route requires a CSRF token: it is only ever called from the editor, and every in-app caller sends one already. A failed fetch returns 400 (not 500) with an empty items array.

get.description:
Serves an external image through the server so the page CSP does not have to allow third-party hosts.

This is NOT an open proxy. Both url and sig are required, and sig must be the HMAC this backend produced when it rewrote the image URL into a feed result. An unsigned or mis-signed URL is refused with 403 before any outbound request is made. Clients therefore never construct this URL themselves — they use the value already present in FeedItem.image.

Responses are served inline with a one-day immutable cache, nosniff, no referrer and a default-src 'none' CSP.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The image URL, exactly as it appeared in the signed link.

parameters.name: sig
parameters.description: HMAC produced by this backend. Bound to the url; not transferable.

403.description: Signature absent or invalid — the URL was not signed by this backend.

502.description: The upstream host could not be reached or returned something unusable.

Note the failure convention: this endpoint answers 200 with an empty list when the connection is missing, the token is absent or the upstream call fails. It never distinguishes those cases, because doing so would let any logged-in user probe which connections exist and whether their credentials still work.

As with the other pickers, any failure answers 200 with an empty list.

Administrators only.

post.description:

RETRY SAFETY. Each item is convergent, so re-sending the same request after a partial failure is safe: a page already deleted counts as deleted, and a page already under the target parent counts as moved. A client that retries the whole batch therefore converges rather than double-counting or erroring. There is no server-side ledger of what a previous call did — the guarantee comes from each item being idempotent, not from request de-duplication.

At most 100 page ids per call; more returns 400. This is a hard service limit, not a page size — there is no continuation token. A migration splits its own work into batches.

RETRY SAFETY. Each item is convergent, so re-sending the same request after a partial failure is safe: a page already deleted counts as deleted, and a page already under the target parent counts as moved. A client that retries the whole batch therefore converges rather than double-counting or erroring. There is no server-side ledger of what a previous call did — the guarantee comes from each item being idempotent, not from request de-duplication.

Three moves are refused per page and reported as that page's failure, not as a request error:
- into itself or one of its own descendants (it would detach the subtree),
- across languages — language folders are independent content trees, so this would be a relocation between intranets rather than a translation,
- the homepage, which is protected.

An empty targetParentId is rejected as a 400 here. Note that the underlying move treats an empty target as 'the root of the page's own language', but this endpoint requires an explicit parent.

Readable by any user with IntraVox access.

post.description:
Installs the bundled demo pages for one language. Administrators only.

The source is chosen automatically: bundled demo data if this build ships it for the language, otherwise a remote download. The two paths do not honour the same options — mode is applied only on the bundled path; a remote import always behaves as overwrite.

An unrecognised mode is silently coerced to 'overwrite' rather than rejected. Given that overwrite is the destructive one, a typo in this field costs content.

post.description:
DESTRUCTIVE AND IRREVERSIBLE. Deletes every page, the navigation and the footer for one language, then creates a fresh homepage with a NEW uniqueId. Comments are deleted too.

There is no dry run, no confirmation parameter and no undo. The new homepage id differs from the old one, so any external deep link into the old homepage breaks.

Administrators only. Scoped to a single language: other languages are untouched.

get.description:
Compares the directories physically present under __groupfolders/ against the GroupFolders registered in the database, and reports the ones with no owner.

This walks the data directory and sizes each candidate, so it is proportional to what is on disk rather than to the number of orphans found.

Administrators only, and deliberately so: these endpoints read and write the raw data directory outside any GroupFolder permission model.

Everything the scan returns for this folder, plus a per-language breakdown in languageDetails.

404 means the id is not orphaned — which includes the case of a folder that is perfectly healthy and still registered. It is a refusal to operate on live data, not only a 'not found'.

Administrators only, and deliberately so: these endpoints read and write the raw data directory outside any GroupFolder permission model.

404.description: Not orphaned, or not accessible. A registered, in-use folder also lands here.

delete.summary: Delete an orphaned folder and everything in it
delete.description:
DESTRUCTIVE AND IRREVERSIBLE. Recursively deletes the directory and its contents from disk. There is no trash, no dry run and no undo.

The one safety net is that the service re-checks the folder is genuinely orphaned before deleting; a registered folder is refused with success:false rather than removed. Inspect with GET /api/orphaned/{id}/details first — that is the only way to see what you are about to destroy.

Administrators only, and deliberately so: these endpoints read and write the raw data directory outside any GroupFolder permission model.

Accepts any language this site treats as IntraVox content: the discovered translations, whatever an administrator has enabled, and the legacy nl/en/de/fr defaults. A language folder from a language that was later disabled stays recoverable, which is the point — otherwise content would be stranded on disk by a setting changed after the fact.

get.description:

No credentials are returned — only the 'connected' flag, the token type and when it was linked.

post.summary: Begin an OAuth2 link for a connection
post.description:
Returns the authorisation URL the browser must be sent to. This endpoint does NOT redirect — it hands back a URL and the caller navigates or opens a popup.

The URL carries a signed state parameter: an HMAC over the connection id, the user id, a timestamp and a 16-character nonce, valid for 10 minutes and accepted once. That binding is what stops an authorisation code from being replayed or attached to a different user, so the URL must be used as given — altering the state invalidates it.

The flow completes at GET /api/lms/callback, which is a browser redirect target rather than an API endpoint: it returns an HTML page that postMessages the opener and is therefore not documented here.

Only for connections whose authMode is not 'token'; a token-mode connection returns 400 and should use POST /api/lms/token/{connectionId} instead.

200.description: Authorisation URL to send the browser to.

authUrl.description: Use verbatim; the state parameter is signed.

400.description: The connection uses authMode 'token' and has no OAuth2 flow, or its client id and secret are not configured.

404.description: No such connection.

500.description: The flow could not be started.

post.summary: Store a manually issued API token
post.description:
Stores an API token the user obtained from the LMS themselves — a Moodle web-service token, for example. The alternative to the OAuth2 flow, for connections whose authMode is 'token'.

The token is VALIDATED BEFORE IT IS STORED by making a live test call against the LMS. A token that does not work, or lacks the required permissions, is rejected with 400 and nothing is saved — so a success here means the token actually functioned at least once.

The token is stored per user and is never returned by any endpoint afterwards; GET /api/lms/connections only reports that one exists.

400.description: Token missing, or the live validation call failed.

404.description: No such connection.

500.description: The token could not be stored.

delete.summary: Remove this user's token for a connection

Deletes the calling user's stored token. Affects only that user — the connection itself stays configured and other users keep their links.

Convergent: disconnecting a connection the user was never linked to succeeds rather than erroring, so a retry is safe.

200.description: Disconnected, or was already not connected.

500.description: The token could not be removed.

get.description:
The complete reaction state for one comment.

Access is checked against the PAGE the comment belongs to, not the comment itself. A comment on a page the caller may not read answers 404 — the same response as a comment that does not exist, deliberately, so the endpoint cannot be used to probe which comment ids are real.

parameters.description: Numeric id of the comment, as a string.

post.description:
Adds the calling user's reaction and returns the complete new state.

Idempotent: adding a reaction the user already has, or removing one they never had, succeeds and returns the unchanged state. Safe to retry, and safe to fire from an optimistic UI.

Access is checked against the PAGE the comment belongs to, not the comment itself. A comment on a page the caller may not read answers 404 — the same response as a comment that does not exist, deliberately, so the endpoint cannot be used to probe which comment ids are real.

Rate limited to 30 per minute per user.

A client that treats this as purely additive will show a stale count for the emoji that was just removed, which is why every reaction endpoint returns the complete state instead of a delta: replace your local state, never increment it.

get.description:
The People widget's data for a publicly shared page.

Anonymous, but not unauthenticated: the share token IS the credential. A password-protected share additionally needs the session cookie from POST /s/{shareToken}/authenticate — without it this answers 403 like an invalid token, so a client must complete that handshake first.

An invalid, expired or unauthorised token yields 403 with {"error": "Invalid or expired share token"}. That is the same answer for 'never existed' as for 'expired', deliberately.

A TOKEN PROVES THE VISITOR MAY READ A PAGE, NEVER THAT THEY MAY QUERY WHAT IS BEHIND IT. Every parameter that selects data is intersected with what the shared page actually publishes; anything beyond that set is dropped rather than honoured.

Concretely: userIds is intersected with the users the widget publishes, and a request naming only unpublished users returns an empty result rather than an error. filters are objects and cannot be intersected element-wise, so the page must publish that EXACT filter set — anything else returns empty.

The viewer-facing facet parameters are not accepted at all. A facet panel on a public share would be a browsable directory of the organisation — roles, buildings, departments and their headcounts — handed to anyone with the link.

The whole endpoint can be switched off instance-wide; when it is, it returns an empty result rather than an error, so a widget degrades to empty instead of breaking the page.

parameters.description: Comma-separated user ids. Intersected with the published set; unpublished ids are silently dropped.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: JSON array of {fieldName, operator, value}. Must match a filter set the page publishes exactly, or the result is empty.

200.description: Matching users. Also the answer when the request was refused for publishing reasons, or when public People is disabled instance-wide — an empty set, never an error.

403.description: Invalid, expired or password-gated share token.

This matters more here than anywhere else, because connectionId selects a STORED connection — credentials and all — and the fetch runs server-side with them. A connectionId the page does not publish is refused with 403 rather than fetched; without that, any share token would drive any configured connection.

The same applies to the RSS url. Note the key asymmetry if you are reading the stored widget: the request parameter is 'url', the published value is stored under 'feedUrl'.

The share token gates access to the endpoint; the signature is what keeps it from being an open proxy. Both apply — a valid token does not make an unsigned URL fetchable.

The custom metadata fields MetaVox defines for the IntraVox group folder.

post.description:
Restores pages, media, comments, navigation and footer from an archive produced by the export endpoints. Administrators only.

This is the ingest path a migration uses. Note what it does NOT have: no dryRun, no idempotency key, and no resume. Re-running it is governed entirely by the overwrite flag — off, existing pages are skipped and counted; on, they are replaced. A partial import leaves what it managed to write.

The upload is checked three ways before anything is read: the MIME type must be a ZIP type, the first two bytes must be PK, and the archive is expanded through a guarded extractor rather than a plain unzip. A file that merely ends in .zip does not get through.

- 400 with errorCode and params: the archive was rejected during validation. These messages are safe to show a user verbatim — they describe the upload, never internal paths. errorCode is stable and translatable; error is an English fallback for scripts.
- 500 with errorId: something went wrong inside. The message is deliberately generic; the errorId correlates with the server log, so quote it in a bug report rather than the message.
- 403: not an administrator.

depublishedOnField.description: MetaVox field name for expiration date

widgetTypes.description: List of widget types used in template

TemplateSaveRequest.description: Body for POST /api/templates. The field names are the ones the handler reads; an earlier version of this schema named pageId/name/description, which the endpoint rejects with 400.

pageUniqueId.description: uniqueId of the page to save as a template.

ViewerFilters.description: Viewer-side facet configuration. When enabled, readers can narrow the widget's own results. Never applied on public share links.

enabled.description: Whether visitors may filter this widget's results.

facets.description: Fields offered as filter groups, in display order.

label.description: Label shown to visitors; falls back to the field's own label.

searchFields.description: Fields the free-text box searches. Display name is always included.

layout.description: Panel beside or above the results.

Translation.description: Another language version of a page, from its translation group. Filtered against the caller's own Team Folder access.

PagedPageSummaries.description: Returned ONLY when the caller paginates explicitly. Without a limit or cursor the endpoint answers with a bare array, unchanged.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or null when the walk is finished — so a loop on `while nextCursor` terminates without a special case. Do not construct or do arithmetic on this value: it encodes the sort key and may change.

StoryPagination.description: Offset paging, as the story widgets use it. Unlike the page listing this one does count rows, because a gallery scrolls a stable snapshot rather than walking a mutating tree.

total.description: Total matching rows, or the configured display limit when one caps the set.

truncated.description: True when a scan cap stopped the count short, so `total` is a lower bound.

StoryCapabilities.description: What the server can do for this source: which optional backends are present.

MetaVoxFieldList.description: MetaVox is optional. When it is absent the endpoint answers 200 with an empty list and available=false rather than an error, so a widget can render without it.

FileStoryListing.description: Documents for the file-story widget. `timeline`+`granularity` appear only when mode=timeline; `groups` only when mode=grouped with a groupBy.

sourceIsFederated.description: Whether the source folder lives on a federated share.

PhotoStoryListing.description: Photos for the photo-story widget. The shape varies with `mode`: on-this-day returns photos+title without pagination, while timeline, grid and highlights go through the paged path and add `pagination`. Mode-specific extras (timeline groups, clusters) appear only for their mode.

title.description: A suggested heading derived from the set.

map.description: Map display settings, when geodata is available.

PhotoClusterListing.description: Geographic clusters for the map view.

truncated.description: True when the scan cap stopped short of the whole set.

PhotoExif.description: EXIF for one photo. Keys depend on what the file carries, so the set is open.

SuccessAck.description: A bare acknowledgement. Failures arrive as a 4xx with an error body, never as success:false here.

SettingsSaveResult.description: Settings write. Returns the stored settings, so a client does not need a follow-up GET to learn what was actually persisted after validation.

VideoDomainsSaveResult.description: Video-domain allow-list write. Entries that failed validation are named rather than silently dropped.

FeedTokenState.description: The RSS token state. `token` is only present right after issuing or regenerating one; a plain read never returns it again.

PageMetadata.description: MetaVox field values for one page. Keys are field ids configured on the instance, so the set is open by nature.

retentionDays.description: Clamped to 7..365 by the handler; a value outside that range is silently brought inside it rather than rejected.

AnalyticsStats.description: View statistics. The metric keys come from the storage layer and vary with what has been collected, so the set is open.

period.description: The window in days that was actually applied, after clamping.

PageLock.description: Who holds the editing lock on a page, or null when it is free.

displayName.description: Shown to the user who is blocked, so they know whom to ask.

lockedSince.description: Unix timestamp the lock was taken.

lastHeartbeat.description: Last refresh. A lock whose heartbeat has gone stale can be taken over.

error.description: Present on a refusal, naming the reason.

LanguageList.description: Which languages exist on the instance and which of them are enabled.

LanguageEnableResult.description: Result of changing the enabled set. Enabling a language creates its homepage, and that can partly fail without the whole call failing — hence the per-language results.

enabled.description: The enabled set after the change.

homepageResults.description: Per newly enabled language, whether its homepage could be created.

LanguageContentStatus.description: Per language, whether it has content yet. The only endpoint here a non-admin may call, because the editor needs it to offer a language switch.

LicenseStats.description: Subscription state and page usage. The verdict comes from the cached result of the last check, not from a live call to the licence server: this is read on every render of the admin settings, and a slow server would otherwise stall the page.

hasLicense.description: Whether a key is configured at all.

licenseReason.description: Why a key was refused — expired, unknown, already registered elsewhere, deactivated. Empty when the licence is valid.

licenseValidUntil.description: Expiry date, also present on a refusal so an expired key can name the date it lapsed.

licenseKeyMasked.description: The key with its middle replaced; the full key is never returned.

freeLimit.description: Pages per language allowed without a subscription.

LicenseValidation.description: The licence server's verdict. Contacts the server, so unlike the stats endpoint it can be slow or fail.

FeedItem.description: One normalised entry. Every source type (RSS, Atom, Moodle, Canvas, Brightspace, Jira, SharePoint, OpenProject, generic REST) is mapped onto this same shape, so a client never branches on sourceType to read a result.

id.description: Source-supplied identifier — a GUID, a link, or an md5 of the title when the feed offers neither. Stable enough to de-duplicate a single fetch; not a durable key.

url.description: Absolute link to the item at its source. Jira issue keys and OpenProject work packages are rewritten to their browse/web URL rather than the API URL.

excerpt.description: Sanitised plain-text summary; source HTML is stripped.

image.description: Never the source URL. Images are rewritten to a signed GET /api/feed/image proxy link, because the page CSP forbids loading third-party images directly. The signature is bound to the URL, so it cannot be pointed elsewhere.

FeedResult.description: Result of a feed fetch. Note the failure convention: an unreachable or malformed source is NOT reported as an item-level error — it returns an empty items array with an error string, so a widget degrades to empty rather than breaking the page.

items.description: Capped at 50 server-side regardless of the requested limit.

source.description: Display name of the origin — the connection name, or the feed's own title for RSS.

feedImage.description: Feed-level logo, proxied the same way as item images.

error.description: Present only on failure, alongside an empty items array.

NamedRef.description: An id/name pair used by every picker endpoint (courses, forums, Jira projects, SharePoint lists). Sorted case-insensitively by name.

FeedConnection.description: A configured external connection. IMPORTANT: this endpoint is available to every logged-in user, because the widget editor needs connection NAMES to build a dropdown. The credential-adjacent fields below are therefore returned ONLY to administrators; a non-admin caller receives the object without them. Never assume their presence.

type.description: moodle, canvas, brightspace, jira, sharepoint, openproject or a generic REST type.

hasToken.description: Whether a token is stored. The token itself is never returned.

hasClientCredentials.description: Whether both a client id and secret are stored. The secret is never returned.

responseMapping.description: Field mapping for generic REST sources. Non-LMS connection types only.

customHeaders.description: Administrators only, non-LMS types only. Routinely holds an API key as a header value — the most sensitive field in this object.

StatusOk.description: A bare acknowledgement using the status/ok convention. Distinct from SuccessAck ({success: true}) — the codebase carries both shapes and they are not interchangeable.

BulkValidation.description: Outcome of a dry run. This is also what a mutating endpoint returns when dryRun is true — note that the envelope then differs from the one you get for the real call, so a client must branch on which it asked for.

success.description: Always true: this reports on the validation itself, not on whether every page passed. Read canProceed and willFail for that.

reason.description: 'Permission denied' or 'Page not found'. Deliberately coarse — it must not confirm the existence of a page the caller may not see.

BulkResult.description:
Outcome of an executed bulk operation.

WATCH THE SUCCESS-COUNT KEY. It is named after the operation, not fixed: 'deleted' for delete, 'moved' for move, 'updated' for update. There is no single key holding the number that succeeded, so a client must look up the one matching the operation it requested. The failure count is always 'failed'.

'failed' is therefore an INTEGER at the top level while results[] entries carry a status string — the two are unrelated despite the shared word.

success.description: True only when nothing failed. A partial result is false and arrives with status 207.

deleted.description: Present only when operation is delete.

moved.description: Present only when operation is move.

updated.description: Present only when operation is update.

results.description: Per-page outcome, successes first then failures.

errors.description: Flat 'pageId: reason' strings, the same failures as in results[]. Redundant, kept for existing callers.

DemoDataStatus.description: Whether demo content is installed, per language.

available_languages.description: Enabled content languages. Note the snake_case keys here — this response mixes conventions with the camelCase setupComplete below.

setupComplete.description: Whether the IntraVox GroupFolder exists yet. When false every language reports status 'setup_required'.

status.description: setup_required: the GroupFolder does not exist. unavailable: no bundled demo data ships for this language. not_installed: nothing there yet. empty: a folder exists but holds no content. installed: content present.

DemoDataOperationResult.description:
Result of an import or clean start.

MIND THE KEY: on this envelope the human-readable text is 'message', both on success and on failure. That differs from the 'error' key returned when the controller itself catches an exception — so a client reading only one of the two will silently show nothing for half the failure modes.

Also note that success:false arrives with HTTP 500, including for ordinary refusals such as 'language not enabled'. That is not a server fault, but it is not distinguishable from one by status code alone.

skipped.description: Pages left alone because they already existed. Import only, and only meaningful in skip_existing mode.

errors.description: Per-page failures. success is true only when this is 0. Import only.

uniqueId.description: Unique id of the freshly created homepage. Clean start only.

OrphanedFolder.description: A directory under __groupfolders/ with no matching GroupFolder row — content left behind when a GroupFolder was removed while its files stayed on disk.

id.description: The numeric folder id, which is also the directory name.

path.description: Absolute server path. Administrator-only information by nature.

hasIntraVoxContent.description: Whether language folders with a home.json were found. False means this orphan is probably not IntraVox's.

sampleContents.description: A capped sample of top-level entries, with totalEntries giving the true count.

languageDetails.description: Per-language breakdown. Returned by the details endpoint only.

LmsUserConnection.description: An LMS connection as seen by ONE user. Distinct from FeedConnection: that describes the admin-level configuration, this describes whether the calling user has personally linked their account to it. Two users see different 'connected' values for the same connection.

authMode.description: 'token' for a manually pasted API token, otherwise an OAuth2 mode. Determines which of the two connect endpoints applies.

oidcAutoConnect.description: Whether the connection reuses the user's existing Nextcloud OIDC session instead of a separate authorisation.

connected.description: Whether this user has a stored token. The token itself is never returned.

connectedAt.description: When this user linked the connection.

PageExport.description: One exported page. Wrapped rather than flat: the page's own document sits under 'content', with comments and reactions alongside it.

content.description: The complete page document as stored.

pageReactions.description: Present only when includeComments is 1 — reactions ride along with comments, they are not separately selectable.

LanguageExport.description:
A complete language export: every page the caller's mount exposes, plus the navigation and footer.

The version fields matter for round-tripping. exportVersion/schemaVersion identify the payload format, and requiresMinVersion states the oldest IntraVox that can import it — an older instance should refuse rather than import partially.

requiresMinVersion.description: Oldest IntraVox version able to import this payload.

pages.description: Each entry carries the page document plus _exportPath and _fileId helpers used on import.

metaVox.description: MetaVox field definitions, when that app is present.

UserProfile.description: A user as this API exposes them. Only the always-present keys are listed; the rest depend on the subject's visibility scopes and on what the directory syncs.

email.description: null when the user's scope hides it. Never read around the scope.

birthdate.description: Normalised to ISO 8601 regardless of how Nextcloud stored it.

ImportStats.description:
What an import actually did. Every counter is an integer — including navigationImported and footerImported, which are 0 or 1 rather than booleans, deliberately so the whole object has one type.

There is no per-page list: a page that was skipped is counted, not named. To know WHICH pages already existed you compare before and after yourself.

pagesSkipped.description: Pages left alone because they already existed and overwrite was off.

metavoxEnabled.description: Whether the archive carried MetaVox data at all.

SafeError.description:
The error shape used where a failure must not describe itself.

'error' is a fixed generic sentence — it never carries the exception message, because these handlers touch file paths and comment ids that would disclose internal structure. The detail is logged server-side under 'errorId'; quote that in a support request rather than the message, which says the same thing every time.

error.description: Generic and stable. Not the cause.

errorId.description: Correlates this response with the server log entry holding the real cause.

ExportableLanguage.description: A content language that can be exported, with enough context to choose one.

FeedSourceType.name: sourceType
FeedSourceType.description: Selects which fetcher runs. Anything other than 'rss' reads connectionId instead of url.

FeedUrl.name: url
FeedUrl.description: RSS/Atom feed URL. Used only when sourceType is rss. Validated against SSRF before any request is made: non-http(s) schemes, loopback, link-local and private ranges are refused, and a host that does not resolve is refused rather than fetched.

FeedConnectionIdQuery.name: connectionId
FeedConnectionIdQuery.description: Which stored connection to fetch through. Used for every sourceType except rss.

FeedCourseId.name: courseId
FeedCourseId.description: A value failing this pattern is silently discarded rather than rejected — the fetch proceeds without a course filter.

FeedContentType.name: contentType
FeedContentType.description: Which slice of the source to read; meaning depends on sourceType. An unrecognised value is silently discarded.

FeedJiraProject.name: jiraProject
FeedJiraProject.description: Jira project key. Silently discarded if malformed.

FeedListId.name: listId
FeedListId.description: SharePoint list or document-library id. Silently discarded if malformed.

FeedSortBy.name: sortBy
FeedSortBy.description: An unrecognised value falls back to 'date' rather than erroring.

FeedSortOrder.name: sortOrder
FeedSortOrder.description: An unrecognised value falls back to 'desc'.
